prose.text: DataChart takes an array of objects in `data` and provides various visualization capabilities on that data. It attempts to default as much as it possibly can to make it easy to get started and then customize later. What follows is some guidance on how to get started and then delve into what DataChart can do.

prose.title: series
prose.text:
To begin with, give your DataChart some data and set the `series` property to indicate which properties in the data objects should be used.

Note that the X and Y axis are defaulted and the dates are automatically formatted based on the granularity given.

prose.title: chart
prose.text: Next, we can customize the kind of chart we are looking at.

prose.title: axis and guide
prose.text: Next, we can customize the axis and add guide lines.

prose.title: React/DOM Properties
prose.text:
At its core, the DataChart component is a regular <div> element. Thus, both DOM and React properties, methods, and events are accessible. To read up on all of the possible DOM attributes and types available for div elements, check out this [MDN Web Documents page.](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/div) To learn more about DOM events and methods, you can read more on the [MDN Web Events documentation page](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Events).

Also, feel free to read about the [types of React events available](https://reactjs.org/docs/handling-events.html), or see [how DOM attributes change in React.](https://reactjs.org/docs/dom-elements.html) Working in tandem with Styled Components, you also have access to the [as property.](https://styled-components.com/docs/api#as-polymorphic-prop)

If 'x' or 'y' is a string, it indicates the property to use to determine the values to show. If 'x' is true, DataChart will look for a property called 'date' or 'time' and automatically use that for the x-axis. 'granularity' indicates how many values to show. If DataChart can't find a property to use, it will use the data index for the x-axis. If axis or 'y' is true, DataChart will use the first property in 'series'. 'coarse' granularity shows two values, one at each end. 'fine' granularity shows all x-axis values and 5 y-axis values. 'medium' granularity picks something in between.
